text:
Noah: Hi all, fresh hire here. On Linux (Ubuntu 22.04) using company WireGuard. Internal k8s API (172.19.4.10) times out from my dev laptop but `kubectl` via bastion works. Docker containers also complain when they try to hit 172.19.x.x. anyone seen docker bridge vs vpn route collisions?
IT-ops: welcome Noah! do `ip route` and `docker network ls && docker network inspect bridge` pls. my guess: dockers default bridge is overlapping an internal subnet or Docker is NATing traffic incorrectly.
Noah: pasted quick output:
```
$ ip route
default via 192.168.1.1 dev wlp3s0 proto dhcp metric 600
172.19.0.0/16 dev wg0 proto kernel scope link
172.17.0.0/16 via 172.17.0.1 dev docker0
$ docker network inspect bridge | jq '.[0].IPAM.Config'
[
  {
    "Subnet": "172.17.0.0/16",
    "Gateway": "172.17.0.1"
  }
]
```
Noah: when I `curl 172.19.4.10` from host it hangs. from a container it errors immediately with "network unreachable".
dev-support-bot: Note: your wg client IP 10.4.12.9, policy split-tunnel. internal k8s API 172.19.4.10 is routed via wg0. Docker bridge 172.17.0.0/16 shouldn't conflict unless containers try to NAT-through host incorrectly.
Dina: Two likely problems: (1) container namespaced networking doesn't have route for 172.19/16, or (2) Docker is configured to masquerade traffic and kernel routing rules prefer docker0 for that range. Quick test: run `docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint bash -it busybox` and try `curl 172.19.4.10` — if host can reach but bridged container can't, it's a Docker bridge issue.
Noah: did `docker run --rm --network host busybox wget -qO- http://172.19.4.10` and it also hangs. but `curl` from host (after `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1`) still hangs until I add an ip rule.
Carlos: interesting. any nft/iptables rules from Docker that might DNAT internal ranges? show `sudo iptables -t nat -L -n -v` and `sudo nft list ruleset`
Noah: iptables NAT has MASQUERADE for 172.17.0.0/16 but nothing touching 172.19.0.0/16. nft output small; nothing obvious.
IT-ops: if the host kernel chooses wrong source interface for replies to 172.19.x (maybe replying via docker0 instead of wg0) packets can get dropped. check `ip rule` and `ip route get 172.19.4.10 from 172.17.0.2` to see which route is chosen for container-sourced traffic.
Noah: `ip route get 172.19.4.10 from 172.17.0.2` returns via 172.17.0.1 dev docker0. aha.
Dina: that means kernel prefers docker0 for containers. Two fixes: (A) configure Docker to use a non-conflicting subnet (recommended long-term) by setting /etc/docker/daemon.json { "bip": "192.168.200.1/24" } and restart docker, or (B) add a source-based route so container traffic to 172.19/16 uses wg0. Example commands (run as root):
```
ip rule add from 172.17.0.0/16 table 200
ip route add default dev wg0 table 200
```
Dina: option B is quick but we prefer A for stable dev environments. We tag new hires who need it with `docker-bip-reassign` for onboarding (ticket ONB-5400) so IT can provision a default non-overlapping bridge.
Noah: I tried changing daemon.json to 192.168.200.1/24, restarted docker, and containers can now curl the k8s API.
IT-ops: great! we'll add ONB-5400 to your onboarding ticket so provisioning uses that bip for similar future VMs. also adding a docs blurb to onboarding about avoiding 172/16 overlaps with internal 172.19.
dev-support-bot: Tip: if you use docker-compose or minikube, explicitly set the network ranges in project configs to avoid surprises.
Noah: thanks all. one more Q: should I keep host ip_forward enabled?
Carlos: we usually leave ip_forward on for dev boxes. if you want it sticky: add `net.ipv4.ip_forward=1` to /etc/sysctl.conf. Security team ok with that for managed laptops.
Noah: beautiful, thanks for the quick help and warm welcome :rocket:
